# Professions of the Beleaguered Present

## The design rule

> status: ratified (D-0018, D-0031, D-0049)

The world must be real-world rich in demographics and industry, populated by people
whose trades are drawn from medieval and pre-Christian Northern European — especially
British Isles — life and lore, and every trade must be legible through the (never
explicit) lens of 21st-century class conflict: gig precarity, externalized costs,
criminalized self-sufficiency, informal unions.

## The trades

> status: provisional (D-0031)

The approved set, each folklore-rooted and class-filtered:

- **Keeners** — professional mourners (the Irish *bean chaointe*): emotional labor as
  a trade; hired to discharge a community's stagnant grief before it curdles. Fiercely
  autonomous; paid in copper and iron; the closest thing sorrow has to a union.
- **Sin-eaters** — the gig-economy of harm absorption: the desperate poor paid to take
  a household's small paradoxes into their own bodies. Shortened lives, externalized
  costs made flesh.
- **Corpse-road drovers** — logistics workers of the old paths: they move flocks and
  contraband along routes the empire doesn't tax, navigating by strict spirit
  etiquette instead of maps. Paranoid, indispensable, unlicensed.
- **Turf-cutters** — the peat proletariat: fuel for everyone, lung-rot for them, and
  an occupational hazard of digging up what the past deliberately buried.
- **Hedge-smiths** — unlicensed menders in a world where the empire monopolizes iron
  and criminalizes repair: the right-to-repair underground in medieval dress.
- **Knot-tiers and midwives** — keepers of fragmentary textile wards and
  birth-protections; practitioners of a decentralized care system the empire cannot
  tax and therefore hunts ([[womens-lives]]).
- **Vellum-scrapers** — the toxic-industry underclass feeding the scriptoriums'
  hunger for parchment: despised by the pious, poisoned by the work, wholly dependent
  on the wage.
- **Muck-larkers** — scavengers of what the shifting bogs disgorge: first to die of
  the old troubles, first to find the old truths, supplier of relics to everyone.
- **Skalds and memory-keepers** — the criminalized oral historians; carrying the old
  axioms in rhyme built to resist corruption. Being one is a capital offense; hiding
  one is a commonplace heroism.

## Fragment-holders

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Most practitioners of the old ways hold fragments without the theory: the smith who
knows one three-syllable charm against rust and dares not change a vowel; the
grandmother who nails iron over doors without knowing why it grounds what it grounds.
Degraded knowledge — superstition — is the fossil record of the true logic, and
reading it correctly is one of the protagonist's arts.

## The cunning-woman's materia

> status: ratified (D-0146)

The cunning-woman's green-lore runs deep and stays material: simples and poultices,
retting-poisons and bog-herbs, each named by its effect and measured by a careful hand. It is
medicine and craft before it is anything mystical, and it doubles as evidence — a plant that
should grow in a place and does not, a water gone quietly wrong, a herb thriving where nothing
should — so reading the green is often the first read of an anomaly ([[anomalies]]). Healing and
poisoning are the same knowledge turned two ways, both costly and both exact; there is no potion
that grants a wish. This is criminalized care, hunted precisely because the empire cannot tax it
([[womens-lives]]).
